context.heading: A wish, not a promise
context.body: John prays that Gaius may "prosper" (euodoō, literally "have a good journey," to get along well) and be in good health. Letters of the time commonly opened with a wish for the reader's health, much like "I hope you're well." It is a warm prayer for a friend, not a guarantee that faithful believers will be wealthy and healthy.

context.heading: Preaching without a price tag
context.body: The missionaries accepted nothing from the ethnikoi ("Gentiles," here meaning pagans outside the faith). Wandering philosophers and religious teachers in the Roman world often begged or charged for their teaching. These Christians refused, so the gospel would not look like a product, which left them dependent on churches like Gaius's.

context.heading: The man who loved first place
context.body: Diotrephes "loves to be first" (philoprōteuō), a rare compound of "loving" and "first." He rejected John's letter, spread malicious nonsense about him, and expelled those who welcomed the missionaries (v. 10). Nothing suggests his teaching was false; his problem was ego, and it split a church.

theology.title: Partners in God's mission
theology.body: Supporting traveling missionaries makes believers "fellow workers for the truth" (v. 8). God has always worked through people who send and people who go: Abraham blessed to bless the nations (Genesis 12:3), the church at Antioch sending Paul (Acts 13:2–3). Those who stay and give are part of the mission, not spectators.

theology.title: For the sake of the Name
theology.body: The missionaries went out "on behalf of the Name" (v. 7). In the Old Testament God's Name stands for His revealed character and presence (Exodus 34:5–7; Deuteronomy 12:5). Early Christians gave the name of Jesus that same weight (Philippians 2:9–11), a quiet witness to His deity.

theology.title: Children resemble their Father
theology.body: "Do not imitate what is evil but what is good" (v. 11). Behavior reveals parentage: whoever does good is of God, and whoever does evil has not seen God. This echoes 1 John 3:10 and Jesus' words that a tree is known by its fruit (Matthew 7:17–20).

application.title: Ambition in church clothes
application.body: Diotrephes probably believed he was protecting his church. Love of first place often hides behind gatekeeping, criticism of outsiders and control over who gets a voice. It shows up in staff meetings, small groups and family decisions.
application.question: Where do you most want to be the one whose opinion settles things?

application.title: Hospitality is ministry
application.body: Gaius welcomed strangers simply because they served Christ, and John calls it faithful work (verse 5). A meal, a spare room or a ride to the airport can be direct partnership in the gospel. Generosity does not need a platform to count.
application.question: Who doing gospel work could you host, feed or practically help this month?

application.title: A reputation built on ordinary days
application.body: Demetrius has a good testimony from everyone, and from the truth itself (verse 12). Character like that is built in unremarkable consistency, seen by believers and outsiders alike. It cannot be rushed or faked for long.
application.question: If the people who see you at your most tired described your character, what would they say?
